Empirical

em-PEER-ih-kul — contains 'peer,' as in looking closely; empirical knowledge comes from actually peering at the evidence. · adjective

Hear It

What It Means

Empirical is based on evidence gathered through observation or experiment.

The professor dismissed the claim outright because it had no empirical support behind it.

Worked Example

A student believes plants grow faster if you talk to them. Instead of just guessing, she plants twenty identical seedlings, talks to half of them daily, and carefully measures their height every week for a month.

Measuring real results instead of just guessing is exactly what makes her conclusion empirical. Unlike 'theoretical,' which is based on ideas alone, empirical means grounded in actual observed evidence.

How Empirical Sits Among Its Neighbors

Synonyms — open each to see how it differs

observed

observed: seen or noted through direct observation

experimental

experimental: based on tests or experiments

factual

factual: based on facts rather than opinion

Antonyms

theoretical

theoretical: based on ideas rather than tested evidence

speculative

speculative: based on guessing rather than evidence

How Strong Is It? — reasonable → empirical → irrefutable

reasonable vs. empirical

reasonable vs. empirical: Reasonable is weaker than empirical — a reasonable guess sounds sensible, but empirical evidence has actually been tested and observed.

irrefutable vs. empirical

irrefutable vs. empirical: Irrefutable is stronger than empirical: empirical evidence has been observed and tested, but irrefutable evidence is so solid it cannot possibly be denied.

Sort It Out

Now place each word on the right side of empirical.

Build the Word

The pieces

Prefix — em-

Prefix — em-: in (the form en- takes before p) (Greek)

Root — pir

Root — pir: trial, experience (from Greek peira, 'trial' -- the same ancient root behind experiment)

Suffix — -ical

Suffix — -ical: relating to (Latin/Greek)

Put it together

Put it together: Em- ('in' -- the shape en- takes before p) + pir ('trial, experience', from Greek peira) + -ical spell empirical. Greek empeirikos meant literally 'in trial': something empirical comes from actually going through the trial or experiment, not from theory alone.

Use the root in a new word: experiment

Use the root in a new word: experiment: The class ran a simple experiment to test whether plants grow faster in sunlight or shade.
